newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat focus switches to option trading.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat focus switches to option trading.

text.p: Options set the pace on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Monday with 40 trades taking place.
No futures were traded as quotes dropped. The settlement market for the most frequently-traded futures contract, January 1997, fell to A$168.50 from Friday's A$174.00.

But 20 call and 20 put options traded on Monday, all in the January 1997 contract. The call options were at a A$200 strike price on a A$1.50 premium, while the puts were at a strike price of A$170 on a A$10.00 premium.
(Call options give the right to convert to a bought futures contract at the strike price. A put gives the right to convert the option to a sold futures contract at the strike price.)
There were no futures trades because no-one wanted to go to A$167.00, the bid for January, Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said.

End users had stepped away from the market entirely, apart from some buying A$200 call options for a hedge after January next year, he said. The put options were likely based on grower hedging, he said.
"It's an excellent volume (in options)," Lindsay said.
